data.name: Chadwick
data.gender_notes: Chadwick is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English words 'cead' meaning 'bold' and 'wic' meaning 'horse', Chadwick is a name of Anglo-Saxon origin that translates to 'bold fighter' or 'warlike horse'. In Christian tradition, it is also associated with the name of Saint Chad, who was a bishop in Mercia in the 7th century. The name Chadwick carries the meaning “Warlike, Fighting horse” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Chadwick usually hope their child will grow to embody warlike, fighting horse and live with faith, good character and purpose.
